planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Cantatrice is a Division 1 trumpet daffodil bred in the Netherlands, prized for its pure white, slightly twisted perianth and long, elegantly flared white trumpet that holds its color without yellowing as it ages. It blooms in mid-spring on sturdy stems and has long been grown as one of the finest all-white trumpet daffodils for borders and naturalizing. Plant bulbs in well-drained soil in full sun in fall, and allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom to recharge the bulb.

common_name: Bravoure Daffodil (Giant White and Yellow Trumpet Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Bravoure is a Division 1 trumpet daffodil with a broad white perianth and a long, softly flared lemon-yellow trumpet, giving a striking bicolor effect on an unusually tall, strong stem. It is a popular modern Dutch introduction widely grown for cutting and mass spring display. Like other large trumpet daffodils, it performs best in full sun and well-drained soil and naturalizes readily in temperate gardens.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Rembrandt is an old Dutch Division 1 trumpet daffodil with a rich, uniform golden-yellow perianth and trumpet, dating to the early twentieth century and still offered by heirloom bulb specialists. Its large, well-proportioned flowers and vigorous growth made it a popular all-yellow trumpet before many modern hybrids were introduced. It naturalizes well in full sun to light shade and increases steadily when left undisturbed.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Daydream is a Division 2 large-cupped daffodil bred by Grant Mitsch, notable for its 'reverse bicolor' coloring: the perianth opens soft yellow and fades to near white while the contrasting cup stays clear yellow. This color-reversal pattern was unusual among daffodils of its era and made Daydream an influential breeding parent as well as a garden favorite. It grows well in full sun on sturdy stems and naturalizes readily in temperate climates.

common_name: Waterperry Daffodil (White Large-Cupped Daffodil with Apricot-Pink Rim)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Waterperry is a Division 2 large-cupped daffodil raised by Irish breeder J. Lionel Richardson, with a creamy white perianth and a frilled cup that opens pale yellow and matures to a delicate apricot-pink rim against a near-white base. It became an important parent in the development of modern pink-cupped daffodils and remains sought after for its subtle coloring. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil for the best pink tones to develop as the flowers age.

common_name: Misty Glen Daffodil (White Large-Cupped Daffodil with Green Eye)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Misty Glen is a Division 2 large-cupped daffodil from Northern Ireland's Carncairn Daffodils, with rounded pure white petals surrounding a pale, lightly frilled cup that shows a soft green eye at its base. It is valued both as a show flower and as a reliable, long-lived garden and naturalizing daffodil. It prefers full sun and moist, well-drained soil during its spring growing season.

common_name: Verger Daffodil (White Small-Cupped Daffodil with Orange-Red Eye)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Verger is a Division 3 small-cupped daffodil with a broad white perianth and a small, flat cup rimmed in bright orange-red, a classic 'eye' pattern long grown in French and English gardens. It is an older cultivar still offered by heirloom and specialist daffodil growers for its vivid color contrast and reliable late-season bloom. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and multiplies steadily once established.

common_name: Mon Cherie Daffodil (White Small-Cupped Daffodil with Pink-Edged Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Mon Cherie is a Division 3 small-cupped daffodil with pure white petals and a frilled cup edged in soft rose-pink, one of the more widely sold pink-cupped daffodils for home gardens. It blooms in mid to late spring and holds its color well in cooler spring weather. Plant in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil for best pink coloring and reliable perennial return.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Colblanc is a Division 3 small-cupped daffodil bred by Northern Irish hybridizer Guy Wilson, who specialized in developing pure white daffodils; its petals and shallow cup are both an unbroken, even white. It was prized as a show flower and breeding parent for its clean color and smooth form. It grows best in full sun and well-drained soil, like other white Wilson-line daffodils.

common_name: Flower Drift Daffodil (Double White and Yellow Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Flower Drift is a Division 4 double daffodil bred by Grant Mitsch, with ruffled white outer segments interspersed with shorter yellow and orange petaloids clustered at the center. The informal, peony-like double form makes it a popular choice for cutting and for extending color in the daffodil border. It performs best in full sun in well-drained soil and benefits from some wind shelter since the heavy double blooms can be top-heavy.

common_name: John Evelyn Daffodil (White Split-Corona Daffodil with Orange Frill)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: John Evelyn is an early split-corona (collar) daffodil with a broad white perianth and a corona split into a ruffled orange-yellow collar that lies nearly flat against the petals. Introduced in the mid-twentieth century by Oregon Bulb Farms, it was among the cultivars that helped popularize the butterfly/split-corona daffodil form now classified as Division 11. It grows vigorously in full sun and is still widely offered for cutting and spring display.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Rippling Waters is a Division 5 triandrus daffodil bred by Grant Mitsch, bearing clusters of two or three nodding, pure white flowers with gracefully reflexed petals on each slender stem. It has been widely used as a breeding parent in developing other white triandrus hybrids prized for their elegant, pendant blooms. It grows best in full sun to light shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Cantabile is a Division 9 poeticus daffodil with pure white, rounded petals surrounding a small, flat cup rimmed in red with a green-tinged throat, echoing the classic pheasant's-eye pattern. It is one of the latest daffodils to bloom each spring, extending the daffodil season after most other divisions have finished flowering. It grows well naturalized in grass or borders in full sun to light shade.

common_name: Panache Daffodil (White Trumpet Daffodil with Pale Lemon Throat)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall before the ground freezes so roots establish ahead of spring bloom.

directions: Panache is a Division 1 trumpet daffodil raised by Irish breeder J. Lionel Richardson, with a creamy white perianth and a long trumpet that opens pale lemon-yellow and whitens as the flower matures. The subtle color shift gives the bloom a refined, two-toned look prized by collectors of trumpet daffodils. It is grown under the same conditions as other large trumpet types: full sun, well-drained soil, and fall planting.
